title: Planned Burn
summary: Execute a known 2 m/s prograde burn and predict how the estimator handles it.

briefing.markdown:
**Situation.** A 2 m/s **prograde** (along-track) burn is scheduled at $t = 1500$ s to raise the orbit. Flight dynamics passes the commanded $\Delta\mathbf v$ to the filter together with an execution uncertainty ($\sigma = 3$ cm/s per axis). The real thruster over-performs by 1% and is mis-pointed by 0.5°.

**Event order.** At 1500 s the simulation (1) propagates to the burn time, (2) applies the impulse — truth gets the *executed* Δv, the filter the *commanded* one — and (3) only then processes the fix stamped 1500 s.

prediction.prompt: What will the innovations look like right after the burn?

options.text: A huge spike — the filter is surprised.
options.feedback: It would be, if the filter didn't know. Here it does.

options.text: Slightly larger than usual for a few fixes, then normal — only the small execution error is a surprise.
options.feedback: Right. The 1% over-performance and 0.5° pointing error are inside the execution uncertainty the filter was told about.

options.text: Exactly zero — the filter knows the burn perfectly.
options.feedback: Execution is never perfect; the filter was given an uncertainty for exactly that reason.

interactive.instructions: Play through the burn with the *Innovations* plot open. In the sandbox panel you can schedule an extra burn yourself.
steps: Watch the velocity uncertainty jump at 1500 s.
Check NIS stays in family after the burn.

objectives.text: Fly through the burn with NIS staying below 4× expected

reasoning.prompt: Why give the filter an execution uncertainty instead of telling it the burn is perfect?

options.text: To make the plots look nicer.
So its covariance admits the burn might differ, letting the following fixes correct the actual Δv.
options.feedback: Yes — the added covariance raises the gain right after the burn so the next fixes can measure the real Δv.

options.text: Because the filter can't add vectors.
options.feedback: It adds the commanded Δv to its velocity estimate directly.

debrief.markdown:
**Known maneuvers are part of the model.** Telling the filter about a burn — with honest execution uncertainty — keeps it consistent through the event.
